h1: Gupta Perioperative Risk for Myocardial Infarction or Cardiac Arrest (MICA) Calculator
summary: Supply the age and the creatinine and the Gupta Perioperative Risk for Myocardial Infarction or Cardiac Arrest (MICA) calculator solves for MICA score. It is built for an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. The formula is printed further down, so you can check the answer by hand if you want to.

sections.title: How does the Gupta Perioperative Risk for Myocardial Infarction or Cardiac Arrest (MICA) calculator work?
sections.html:
The Gupta Perioperative Risk for Myocardial Infarction or Cardiac Arrest (MICA) calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports MICA score in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the status, the ASA Class and the procedure); then you type in the age and the creatinine.

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
• A number, expressed in years.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 3 options, such as totally independent, partially dependent and totally dependent. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 5 options, such as 1: healthy, 2: mild systemic disease and 3: severe systemic disease. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in milligrams per deciliter. The unit chip switches it to any of the 3 supported units.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 21 options, such as anorectal, aortic and bariatric. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.

3 fields on this form are a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the Gupta Perioperative Risk for Myocardial Infarction or Cardiac Arrest (MICA) calculator
sections.html:
One relationship drives the whole page:

MICA score=(100 × the exponential of ((1 ÷ 50) × age + ASA Class + procedure + status + (61 ÷ 100) × rounded up, ((1 ÷ 10) × rounded up, ((1 ÷ 2) × (10, -the absolute value of (creatinine)) × (2 × creatinine − 3))) − 21 ÷ 4) ÷ (the exponential of ((1 ÷ 50) × age + ASA Class + procedure + status + (61 ÷ 100) × rounded up, ((1 ÷ 10) × rounded up, ((1 ÷ 2) × (10, -the absolute value of (creatinine)) × (2 × creatinine − 3))) − 21 ÷ 4) + 1))

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
• A number, filled in as soon as the inputs allow it.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

  • Creatinine, opening in milligrams per deciliter

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Gupta Perioperative Risk for Myocardial Infarction or Cardiac Arrest (MICA) calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Any time the same 2 figures keep coming back — the age and the creatinine — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Gupta Perioperative Risk for Myocardial Infarction or Cardiac Arrest (MICA) calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns MICA score, derived from the age and the creatinine. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Gupta Perioperative Risk for Myocardial Infarction or Cardiac Arrest (MICA) calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the age and the creatinine, which is 5 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter creatinine in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Creatinine opens in milligrams per deciliter and the chip beside it offers 3 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (3 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

faq.q: Is the Gupta Perioperative Risk for Myocardial Infarction or Cardiac Arrest (MICA) calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
